item.title: Malinin made history with his Olympic backflip, but some say the glory was owed to a Black skater
item.description: U.S. figure skater Ilia Malinin has become the first person to legally land a backflip on Olympic ice. He performed the move on Sunday, marking a significant moment in figure skating history. But he's not the first to do the move. The backflip was first landed by Terry Kubicka at the 1976 Olympics but was banned for being too dangerous. item.title: Mikaela Shiffrin’s fourth Olympics begin with a sluggish slalom and a fourth-place finish
item.description: Mikaela Shiffrin extended her Olympic slump with a fourth-place finish in the new team combined event after partner Breezy Johnson led the opening downhill leg. Shiffrin is the most successful World Cup racer of all time with a record 108 victories overall and 71 in slalom but she has now gone seven straight Olympic races without a medal. item.title: Norwegian biathlon bronze medalist confesses to cheating on girlfriend in post-race interview
item.description: Sturla Holm Laegreid, a top Norwegian biathlete, made a surprising revelation during a live broadcast after winning bronze in the men's Olympic biathlon. On Tuesday, he admitted to being unfaithful to his girlfriend, calling it the biggest mistake of his life. Fighting back tears, he described her as the "gold medal" in his life. item.title: Ukraine’s Vladyslav Heraskevych out of Winter Olympics because of banned helmet honoring war dead
item.description: Ukrainian skeleton racer Vladyslav Heraskevych is out of the Milan Cortina Games after he refused to stop wearing a banned tribute helmet. International Olympic Committee President Kirsty Coventry met him at the track before the men’s race for a private talk to make a last-minute plea but Heraskevych refused to change his stance. item.title: What we can learn from lovebirds, the rare birds that mate for life
item.description: Phoenix is believed to be home to the world's largest colony of rosy-faced lovebirds outside of their native Africa. There are about 2,000 lovebirds that have learned to adapt to life in a city known for sweltering summers mainly by sticking close to people and their air conditioning. The pet birds earned their name because of their tendency to form lifelong bonds with their mates, who like to perch close together, almost like they’re cuddling. item.title: Mandatory driver impairment sensors clear a funding hurdle, but are they ready?
item.description: A federal law requires new cars to include technology that detects drunk or impaired driving, but regulators still have not cleared it. Last month, the U.S. House rejected a Republican effort to strip the law’s funding. The law is named after five members of a Michigan family who were struck and killed by a drunk driver in 2019 in Kentucky. item.description: Authorities say four people are dead after a small plane crashed Friday on a mountain near the Colorado ski resort community of Steamboat Springs.
